english.title: Export / attempt to export nuclear material with intent to evade a prohibition / restriction
english.standardoffencewording:

(A)_[exportation]_
(B)_[shipment as stores]_
(C)_[attempted exportation]_
(D)_[attempted shipment as stores]_

of nuclear material, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NUCLEAR MATERIAL..), with intent to evade a

(E)_[prohibition]_
(F)_[restriction]_

as is mentioned in section 68(1) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979, namely **(..SPECIFY PROHIBITION..)

english.notes:
(i) For offences committed on or after 22nd February 2024 refer to H102463. While the maximum penalty for this offence has not changed, section 68(4B) has been omitted and there is therefore no specific penalty for this offence in respect of nuclear material; the increased penalty in section 68(3) applies to offences committed prior to 22nd February 2024.
(ii) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Commissioners for Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs, see section 145 of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
(iii) For forfeiture see section 68(5) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

consent.description: Commissioners of HM Rev and Customs

other.penalty:
Either way:
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a penalty of three times the value of the goods or a fine not exceeding £20,000 whichever is the greater.
Indictment: maximum 14 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex, see section 146A of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
